# Polyfills by dialect

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_polyfill_docs.py from provisa/transpiler/polyfill: do not edit by hand. -->

A polyfill is how Provisa gives a PostgreSQL client PostgreSQL's behaviour on a connector dialect Provisa sends SQL to: a serving engine's, or a source's a statement is sent to directly. Each dialect below has a table of every feature that has a polyfill or a limitation there: its read polyfill, read limitations, write polyfill and write limitations. A feature the dialect does natively with no difference from PostgreSQL is left out and counted. Each dialect's page prints the same table with the rules it runs.

## [PostgreSQL](postgres.md)

17 of the grid's 17 features are native on PostgreSQL and left out.

<table><thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>Read polyfill</th><th>Read limitations</th><th>Write polyfill</th><th>Write limitations</th></tr></thead><tbody>
</tbody></table>

## [DuckDB](duckdb.md)

2 of the grid's 17 features are native on DuckDB and left out.

<table><thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>Read polyfill</th><th>Read limitations</th><th>Write polyfill</th><th>Write limitations</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><strong>array_ndims</strong><br>The number of an array&#x27;s dimensions.</td><td><pre><code>array_ndims($a::anyarray)
=&gt;

<tr><td><strong>array_dims</strong><br>The text of an array&#x27;s dimensions, such as [1:2][1:3].</td><td><pre><code>array_dims($a::anyarray)
=&gt;

<tr><td><strong>array_lower</strong><br>The lower bound of a dimension: 1, as a list&#x27;s index starts there.</td><td><pre><code>array_lower($a::anyarray, $d::integer)
=&gt;
CAST(CASE WHEN $d BETWEEN 1 AND CAST(CASE WHEN len($a) &gt; 0 THEN length(regexp_extract(typeof($a), &#x27;(\[\])+$&#x27;)) // 2 END AS INTEGER) THEN 1 END AS INTEGER)</code></pre></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><strong>array_upper</strong><br>The upper bound of a dimension: its length.</td><td><pre><code>array_upper($a::anyarray, $d::integer)
=&gt;
CAST(CASE WHEN $d BETWEEN 1 AND CAST(CASE WHEN len($a) &gt; 0 THEN length(regexp_extract(typeof($a), &#x27;(\[\])+$&#x27;)) // 2 END AS INTEGER) THEN json_array_length(to_json($a), &#x27;$&#x27; || repeat(&#x27;[0]&#x27;, CAST($d - 1 AS INTEGER))) END AS INTEGER)</code></pre></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><strong>array_length</strong><br>The length of a dimension; NULL for a dimension the array does not have.</td><td><pre><code>array_length($a::anyarray, 1)
=&gt;
CAST(CASE WHEN len($a) &gt; 0 THEN len($a) END AS INTEGER)</code></pre><pre><code>array_length($a::anyarray, $d::integer)
=&gt;
CAST(CASE WHEN $d BETWEEN 1 AND CAST(CASE WHEN len($a) &gt; 0 THEN length(regexp_extract(typeof($a), &#x27;(\[\])+$&#x27;)) // 2 END AS INTEGER) THEN json_array_length(to_json($a), &#x27;$&#x27; || repeat(&#x27;[0]&#x27;, CAST($d - 1 AS INTEGER))) END AS INTEGER)</code></pre></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><strong>array_fill</strong><br>An array of a value repeated to the dimensions given.</td><td><pre><code>array_fill($v::anyelement, $dims::integer[])
=&gt;

=&gt;

<tr><td><strong>array_shuffle</strong><br>An array&#x27;s elements in a random order.</td><td><pre><code>array_shuffle($a::anyarray)

<tr><td><strong>trim_array</strong><br>An array without its last elements.</td><td><pre><code>trim_array($a::anyarray, $n::integer)
